liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (1 review): The Sugaree into Jack Straw pairing was short but especially sweet [20]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet is singled out as a standout, well played and strong [20]
- **Big River** (1 review): Big River in the first set was raucous [24]
- **Willie And The Hand Jive** (1 other source): A noodle leading into Hand Jive is included within the Willie & The Hand Jive track [1]
- **Iko Iko** (1 other source): Possibly the fastest Iko Iko ever played [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd86-12-16 01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 03 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 04 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 05 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 06 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 07 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd86-12-16 08 When Push Comes To Shove**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-12-16.140294.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 144 min [1]
- **gd1986-12-16.139726.sbd.miller.flac2496**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 142 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd86-12-16.sbd.tetzeli.8399.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Jerry's voice comes through clearly on this tape; The tape speed seems slightly different from the other copies [30]
- **gd1986-12-16.sbd.miller.77409.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 3/5 by 10 [4]
- **gd1986-12-16.nak300.damico.88891.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 1.33/5 by 3 [11]. Said about its sound: Punchy yet not harsh, very clear, with some channel separation; Channels seem reversed: Brent is heard in the left headphone and Bob's guitar in the right [27]
- **gd1986-12-16.nakcm304.beckham.suraci.sbeok.80849.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 127 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [13]. Said about its sound: Decent audience recording in which Bob is far forward in the mix, while Jerry's guitar is not hidden [24]

## Around the show

- The show came right after Jerry's return, and the band sounded fresh and re-energized [20]
- The crowd sounded like an east coast crowd, though quieter than the previous night's [24]
- Reviewer traveled from Houston and caught the last two of three comeback shows following Garcia's five-day coma [31]
- The Neville Brothers joined the band from Drums through Iko Iko and In The Midnight Hour [2]
- Guests included Brian Stoltz, Willie Green and Art Neville [4]
- The reviewer considers this the best of the three nights' versions so far, and wants a soundboard like the first night's [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-12-16.140294.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jim Wise, Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 > Oade M118 > Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM (unknown deck/hardware/software) > hard disk > Adobe Audition… [1]
- **gd1986-12-16.139726.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [2]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [2]
- **gd86-12-16.sbd.tetzeli.8399.sbeok.shnf**: source: Src: SBD > ?? > cassette > .wav > CDR > EACed to .wav > .shn [3]. Also: Soundboard source copied through unknown generation to cassette, then wav, CDR, and shn; seeded by Bill Tetzeli [3]
- **gd1986-12-16.sbd.miller.77409.flac16**: taped by Thanks to Paul Scotton and Joani Walker for the Cassettes; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/TDK MX-XG90) D [4]. Also: Tape feeds from Joanie and PSCotton went to Miller for this soundboard release [28]
- **gd1986-12-16.nak300.damico.88891.flac16**: taped by Joe D'Amico; source: nak 300 mics w/cp4 shotguns > sony d-5 > mac [11]
- **gd1986-12-16.nakcm304.beckham.suraci.sbeok.80849.flac16**: taped by Don Beckham and Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304>Sony D5 [13]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1986-12-15 Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1986-12-15-oakland-alameda-county-coliseum-oakland-ca-usa/) [33]
- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1986-12-15 Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1986-12-15-oakland-alameda-county-coliseum-oakland-ca-usa/) [34]

claims.text: The show came right after Jerry's return, and the band sounded fresh and re-energized
The Sugaree into Jack Straw pairing was short but especially sweet
Estimated Prophet is singled out as a standout, well played and strong
Decent audience recording in which Bob is far forward in the mix, while Jerry's guitar is not hidden
The crowd sounded like an east coast crowd, though quieter than the previous night's
Big River in the first set was raucous
Punchy yet not harsh, very clear, with some channel separation
Channels seem reversed: Brent is heard in the left headphone and Bob's guitar in the right
Tape feeds from Joanie and PSCotton went to Miller for this soundboard release
Jerry's voice comes through clearly on this tape
The reviewer considers this the best of the three nights' versions so far, and wants a soundboard like the first night's
The tape speed seems slightly different from the other copies
Reviewer traveled from Houston and caught the last two of three comeback shows following Garcia's five-day coma
Master recordings by the Oade brothers and crew, transferred to hard disk, with Jim Wise's drive and Charlie Miller coordinating
A noodle leading into Hand Jive is included within the Willie & The Hand Jive track
Possibly the fastest Iko Iko ever played
The Neville Brothers joined the band from Drums through Iko Iko and In The Midnight Hour
Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete
Soundboard source copied through unknown generation to cassette, then wav, CDR, and shn; seeded by Bill Tetzeli
Cassettes were supplied by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker
Guests included Brian Stoltz, Willie Green and Art Neville
